_meta.title: Placed LinkedIn scoring rules (draft)
_meta.status: Wired into lib/linkedin-score (v0.1.0-draft). Calibrate weights on real profiles; build >=5 real Save-to-PDF fixtures. Rules with pdfContested: true are not judged from the PDF until then.
_meta.scoreMeaning: LinkedIn readiness for archetype X at year Y: how the profile comes across when a recruiter or contact looks the student up or searches. Not a hiring or employability score, and not comparable with the CV score.

engineFit.types: Severity, Evidence, Citation, Archetype and Year match lib/cv-rules/types.ts and lib/types.ts. Dimension is a new LinkedIn-specific union: integrity | proof | findability | narrative | polish | presence.
engineFit.aggregation: Reuse lib/cv-score/aggregate.ts unchanged in shape: rule weight = SEV {critical 3, major 2, minor 1} x EVID {A 1, B 0.85, C 0.6, D 0.4}; credit pass 1 / partial 0.5 / fail 0; not_applicable and could_not_assess drop out; dimension score = weighted pass share; total = sector-weighted mean over dimensions that have at least one assessed rule (automatic renormalisation).
engineFit.severityPrecedence: yearAdjust > sectorAdjust > base, as effectiveSeverity() already does. yearAdjust.skip drops the rule.
engineFit.sourceIds: Resolve to Citation via sources[] (title, publisher, year, url). The first sourceId is the one shown on the fix card.
engineFit.replacedBy: Scorer drops a generic rule for a sector listed in its replacedBy map; the named sector rule does the job with sector-specific content.
engineFit.advisory: advisory: true rules sit in the presence dimension (weight 0) and render on a separate 'Presence tips' card. They never move the score or trigger caps.
engineFit.riskFlag: riskFlag: true findings render with stronger 'risk' styling. Only integrity-dimension risk rules can cap the score.
engineFit.input: Primary input. altInputs lists other inputs that can also decide the rule. pdf_export = LinkedIn Save to PDF; screenshot = user screenshot (vision/OCR); self_report = user answer or paste.
engineFit.pdfContested: Rule reads a PDF section whose presence in the export is contested (full skills list, Projects, Volunteering, Recommendations). Gate behind real fixtures.
engineFit.evidence: Single letter for the engine. Where a researcher gave a mixed grade (e.g. 'B/D'), the lower grade is used, matching the CV engine's conservative policy; evidenceNote keeps the original grades. Merged rules take the grade best supported by the retained sources (editor's call, explained in evidenceNote).
engineFit.params: Same meaning as CvRule.params: threshold = pass/fail cut-off; majorThreshold = upper bound or escalation level. sectorParams overrides params per archetype (new field).

caps.rule: Any critical rule fails (after year/sector adjustment).
caps.label: Critical issue: capped at 59 until fixed

caps.rule: No About, AND no Experience description of 15+ words, AND headline matches ^Student at.
caps.label: Starter profile: capped at 40

_meta.noCvOnFile: LI-GEN-01 and LI-GEN-04 are not_applicable; integrity is then judged on the remaining integrity rules and renormalisation spreads its weight. UI: 'Upload your CV to unlock the consistency check, the thing recruiters most often catch.'

scorerGuards.noVanityInputs: Never score follower or connection count, post frequency, creator mode, endorsement counts or 'All-Star' status, in any sector (from LI-FINANCE_BANKING-17, generalised; 02 §4).
scorerGuards.noPhotoAppearance: Never assess a photo's appearance, dress, background or 'professionalism'; no face analysis or AI-face detection on users' photos (02 §4.1).
scorerGuards.nonTechDegreeNotPenalised: product: suppress any degree-relevance deduction; technical modules are a bonus (LI-PRODUCT-14; Capital One, Meta).
scorerGuards.noUniversityPrestige: Never encode university prestige into the score (05 myths; Jane Street hires 'from many different universities').
scorerGuards.nonUkExperienceJudgedOnDescription: The LLM must not mark unfamiliar non-UK employers or universities as weak; judge the description, not the brand (02 §4.4).
scorerGuards.protectedCharacteristicsIgnored: LLM prompts ignore name, age, nationality, religion, ethnicity, disability, pronouns and reasons for gaps. Gaps are never penalised; CV/LinkedIn date inconsistency is (02 §4.4).
scorerGuards.zeroPostsNeverFail: No sector fails a profile for not posting. Activity is advisory everywhere except marketing_growth, where substantive posts count as portfolio proof and absence is not_applicable.
scorerGuards.noMultipliersInUi: Never print 'Nx more views' figures in the UI. Qualitative copy only ('LinkedIn says profiles with photos get more views') (01 §5).
scorerGuards.notApplicableNotFail: A rule whose input is missing (no screenshot, no CV, no self-report) is not_applicable and drops out of the denominator; the UI says what would unlock it.
scorerGuards.claimsAreAdvisory: Unverifiable yes/no self-report claims never move the score (answering 'no' must not cost points). Pasted URLs and pasted text are verifiable content and can be scored.
scorerGuards.neverInventAchievements: Rewrite suggestions are grounded in facts from the user's CV and profile; Placed never invents numbers, titles or outcomes.

rules.statement: Consistent with the CV Placed already holds: same employers, equivalent titles, dates within one month, same degree, grade, competition ranks and project metrics. LinkedIn may carry extra detail but must not contradict the CV. Not applicable when no CV is on file.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: D; 02: B; 03: A (general truthfulness); 05: B/C; 06: B/D; 08: D; 09: B; 10: B. Merged at B: no source says outright that recruiters diff the two documents; the logic (interviewers probe every line, Unilever imports LinkedIn into its form) is strong.
rules.llmGuidance: Do the LinkedIn profile and the CV disagree on any employer, job title (beyond synonyms), date (by more than one month), degree, grade, competition rank or project metric? (yes = fail). Extra LinkedIn-only detail is not a contradiction. LinkedIn often splits one CV line into several roles (a promotion, two society terms): roles that sit inside the CV's dates for that organisation agree with it. On fail, show both values and ask 'which is right?'.
rules.passExample: CV and LinkedIn both say 'Summer Analyst, Barclays, Jun-Aug 2026'.
rules.failExample: CV: 'Spring Week participant, Apr 2026'; LinkedIn: 'Investment Banking Analyst, Apr-Jun 2026'. Or CV 'top 10%' vs LinkedIn 'top 1%'.
rules.notes: Needs the stored ParsedCV. Raised to critical for marketing (researcher had major) because a contradiction is misrepresentation in every sector.

rules.statement: No inflated or misleading Experience titles: each title fits the real format, duration and work. Spring weeks, insight days, one-day events and virtual work experience or job simulations (e.g. Forage) are labelled as such; a solo side project is not shown as employment or as 'CEO/Managing Director'.
rules.evidenceNote: 02: A (LinkedIn policy + employer CV guidance). 08: D mirroring CV FCQ-11 (A). 05 (programme labelling): D.
rules.llmGuidance: Given the description, dates and format, is every Experience title a fair label for what the role actually was? A spring week, insight day, one-day event or virtual work experience / job simulation (e.g. Forage) shown with an Intern, Analyst, Trader, Associate or Engineer title at a named employer, or Founder/CEO/MD on a solo project with no users, is not. (no = fail)
rules.passExample: 'Spring Insight Programme, J.P. Morgan (1 week)'; 'Founder, campus tutoring service (40 paying clients)'.
rules.failExample: 'Investment Banking Intern, J.P. Morgan' spanning 3 days; a Forage simulation listed as employment at Goldman Sachs; 'Trading Intern, Optiver' for a one-day insight event; 'Managing Director, Personal Investment Portfolio'.
rules.notes: Quant researcher graded programme labelling major; raised to critical because mislabelling breaches LinkedIn's misrepresentation policy. Self-descriptive headline labels ('Data Scientist', 'AI Researcher') are handled by sector rules at major.

rules.statement: No confidential employer, client or deal information: no non-public client or deal names, internal figures, internal dashboards or customer data, offer or pay details, or assessment and case-interview content.
rules.evidenceNote: 06: D (no firm policy retrieved); 08: D (banks' confidentiality culture, FCA context); 04: D (professional norm, GDPR context). Audit 2026-10-18 (docs/research/audit-2026-10-18/08-linkedin.md): question rewritten to be decidable; a fail must quote the line, and a D-graded LLM verdict never triggers the 59 cap.
rules.llmGuidance: Does any line state (a) a salary or offer amount, (b) an online-assessment or interview question, (c) revenue, P&L or deal value attributed to an employer or client, or (d) text the student labels internal or confidential? Naming an employer or client alone is NOT a fail, and you cannot know what is non-public, so do not guess. (yes = fail; quote the line)
rules.passExample: 'Built trading comps for a mid-cap industrials sell-side process.' / 'Pro-bono project for a London housing charity: built a volunteer-retention model.'
rules.failExample: 'Worked on Project Falcon, the confidential £1.2bn sale of [named company]'; a Featured screenshot titled 'Q3 internal sales dashboard - [Employer]'; 'helped [named client plc] plan 300 redundancies'.
rules.notes: quant_trading uses LI-QUANT_TRADING-01 instead (P&L/strategy pre-filter). Screenshot-only evidence from posts is shown as a risk finding; it still caps because the content is confidential, not merely unflattering.

rules.statement: Profile and CV tell the same story about the target: if the CV targets sector X, the headline and About do not target an unrelated sector Y. LinkedIn may be broader than the CV. Not applicable when no CV is on file.
rules.llmGuidance: Is the career target implied by the LinkedIn headline and About compatible with the target sector of the user's CV? (no = fail)
rules.passExample: CV for quant; LinkedIn 'Maths @ Imperial, interested in quant research and trading'.
rules.failExample: CV for investment banking; LinkedIn headline 'Aspiring UX designer'.

rules.statement: Headline states what the student studies or targets plus at least one concrete differentiator (skill, experience, achievement); it is not just 'Student at X'.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: A, critical; 02: A, major. Editor chose major (critical is reserved for integrity).
rules.llmGuidance: Code flags headlines under 4 words or matching ^Student at. Then ask: does the headline say what field or role the student is targeting AND give at least one concrete differentiator (skill, experience, achievement)?
rules.passExample: 'Maths & CS @ UCL | Python, SQL | Summer analyst intern @ Barclays 2026'
rules.failExample: 'Student at University College London'
rules.notes: Every archetype has a sector headline rule that replaces this one, so it only runs when the user has no archetype yet.

rules.statement: Headline front-loads the key information: the first ~70 characters (what shows in search results, comments and invites) name the field or target role. Length is read from the export, not hard-coded (220 is reported by trade sources; UK careers pages still say 120 or 200).
rules.llmGuidance: Take the first 70 characters of the headline. On their own, do they tell a recruiter the student's field or target role?
rules.passExample: 'Economics BSc (LSE) | Aspiring M&A analyst | Investment Society VP ...'
rules.failExample: '✨ Passionate lifelong learner who loves challenges, people and growth | Economics...' (field appears after character 70)

rules.statement: 'Seeking' language belongs in About or Open to Work, not as the whole headline: a headline that is only 'Seeking opportunities' / 'Aspiring X' / 'Open to work' fails.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: regex ^(seeking|looking for|aspiring|open to) with fewer than 6 other content words. Tie-break: is the headline only a job-seeking statement with no field, skill or experience? (yes = fail)
rules.passExample: 'Seeking 2027 software internships | Java, React | Hackathon winner'
rules.failExample: 'Looking for opportunities'

rules.statement: No keyword stuffing: the headline reads as a phrase a person wrote (at most 4 segments separated by | or •, no term repeated 3 or more times) and the skills list is not padded with unrelated terms. A middot (·) list inside one segment is fine.
rules.evidenceNote: 02: B/D (skill lists add little for raters [Roulin & Levashina]; thresholds are synthesis). Lower grade used. Audit 2026-10-18 (docs/research/audit-2026-10-18/08-linkedin.md): separator count loosened: the playbook's own Good headlines have 4 segments and middot lists.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: count headline segments (split on | and •; a middot list or a slash inside a segment stays one segment) and terms repeated 3+ times.

rules.statement: Education is complete: institution (ideally from LinkedIn's school list), degree and subject, start and expected graduation year. Graduation year is a recruiter filter. Masters students also list their undergraduate degree.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: A, critical; 02: A, major. Editor chose major (critical reserved for integrity).
rules.llmGuidance: Parse the Education block: institution, degree, subject, end year present. For masters, also an undergraduate entry. Grade is checked by sector rules, not here.

rules.statement: Location is set to the UK city or region the student wants to work in (or studies in), not blank or a country they are not targeting. International students targeting the UK are told why; it is never a fail for them to list a home city if they are not targeting the UK.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: A (profile meter + Recruiter location filter); 02: B.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: a blank location fails; a UK place passes; any other location is not applicable (never a fail: the student may not be targeting the UK).

rules.statement: Custom public URL claimed (linkedin.com/in/firstname-lastname style), not the default random suffix, so it can go on the CV.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: A (LinkedIn recommends a name variation); 02: B. Lower used.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: slug from the export's Contact block; fail if it ends in -[0-9a-f]{6,} or a long digit run.

rules.statement: Name field holds the student's name only: no emoji, job titles, 'Open to work', 'Student', 'Hiring' or 'Seeking'. Mononyms, initials and non-Western name orders always pass.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: D, major. Editor lowered to minor and narrowed the regex so it can never penalise how people's names are written.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: fail only on emoji or the words student|hiring|open to work|seeking|intern in the name field.

rules.statement: Skills section is populated: the ~3 Top Skills shown in the export are relevant to the target, and (when a screenshot or pasted list is given) at least 5 and no more than 50 skills are listed.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: A that skills matter (profile meter, matching), D for the threshold (01 said >=10; TARGETjobs says 5-10 key skills). Editor's range 5-50; lower grade used.

rules.statement: Every Experience entry (including part-time, volunteering and society roles) has a description saying what the student personally did and at least one result or scope; no title-only entries.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: D (supported by AI search reading full text); 02: A (TARGETjobs 'I' statements and achievements; Worcester).
rules.llmGuidance: Does every Experience entry (including part-time, volunteering and society roles) say what the student personally did and give at least one result or scope? A title-only entry is a fail.
rules.passExample: 'Ran sign-ups for a 300-person careers fair; cut no-shows 25% with SMS reminders.'
rules.failExample: 'Volunteer.' / 'Various tasks in the office.'

rules.statement: Experience dates are complete and consistent: month and year for start and end; finished roles have end dates; no more than one 'Present' role that is actually over. Gaps are never penalised.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: date parser; flag >1 'Present' role, and an internship marked 'Present' for more than 6 months. Recruiter years-of-experience is computed from these dates.

rules.statement: Listed skills are evidenced: each Top Skill (and any skill the user pastes) appears in use in at least one Experience, Education, Project or About description. At least 50% evidenced to pass.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: D (aligns with semantic AI search); 02: B/D. Lower used.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: string and synonym match of each skill against body text. LLM for paraphrase: is the skill '<skill>' shown being used anywhere in the profile text, even in different words?
rules.passExample: Skill 'Financial Modelling'; Experience: 'Built a 3-statement model for a society stock pitch.'
rules.failExample: Skill 'Machine Learning'; mentioned nowhere else.

rules.statement: At least one work sample is visible: a Featured item, Projects entry, or a link in Contact/About to a project, portfolio, write-up or competition result.
rules.llmGuidance: Pass if the export's Contact/About has a non-LinkedIn work link, or a Featured screenshot / pasted URL shows the student's own work. Not applicable (not fail) when no screenshot is given and the PDF has no link.
rules.passExample: Featured: society stock-pitch deck PDF with the student's section named.
rules.failExample: Featured holds only a LinkedIn Learning certificate image.
rules.notes: Runs for consulting and finance_banking (and users with no archetype); other sectors use stronger sector rules.

rules.statement: About section is present and long enough to say something: at least ~400 characters (sector minimums below). Upper bounds are checked by sector rules.
rules.evidenceNote: Summary is one of LinkedIn's 7 profile-meter sections (A); length bands are synthesis. 01 wanted >=600 chars; 02 wanted 60-300 words; sector files ranged from 300-600 chars (quant) to 2,000 (SWE). Editor: generic floor 400 chars, sector floors as listed.

rules.statement: About opening hook: the first ~250 characters (above 'see more') say who the student is, what they study and what they are aiming for.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: C (fold length, trade sources) / D. Lower used.
rules.llmGuidance: Within the first 250 characters, does the About say what the student studies, where, and what they are aiming for?
rules.passExample: 'I'm a second-year Physics student at Imperial looking for 2027 quant research internships. I've built ...'
rules.failExample: 'Ever since I was young I have always been fascinated by how the world works and the people in it...'

rules.statement: About is specific: what the student studies, at least one concrete, checkable example (project, role, result, number) and a stated target.
rules.llmGuidance: Does the About include at least one concrete, verifiable example (project, role, result) and a stated target?
rules.passExample: '...built a Python model forecasting society ticket demand (±8%)... looking for 2027 data analyst internships.'
rules.failExample: 'Passionate, driven student eager to learn and grow.'
rules.notes: Every archetype has a sector About rule, so this runs only without an archetype.

rules.statement: No cliché-saturated or generic AI-style text: at most 2 clichés (passionate, driven, results-oriented, dynamic, team player, synergy, leverage) without evidence nearby, and the About could not be pasted onto another student's profile unchanged. Placed grades specificity; it never tries to 'detect AI'.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: C/D, minor; 02: C, major (CV doc FCQ-12, eFC 2026). Editor: major.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: cliché density from the lexicon shared with CV rule GEN-09. Then ask: could this About be pasted onto another student's profile in the same sector with only the name changed? (yes = fail)
rules.passExample: Mentions the student's actual modules, projects and societies by name.
rules.failExample: 'Driven and results-oriented individual eager to leverage my skills in a dynamic environment.'
rules.notes: Detecting AI is unreliable and unfair to non-native writers (02 §5).

rules.statement: Spelling and grammar are clean across headline, About and Experience (British and American spellings are both fine), with consistent date formats and title capitalisation.
rules.evidenceNote: 01: A by analogy with CV FCQ-05; 02: A (careers-service consensus). Consulting researcher asked for critical (attention to detail); editor kept major and gave consulting a higher polish weight instead, because critical is reserved for integrity and one spell-checker false positive on a proper noun must not cap the score.
rules.llmGuidance: Are there 3 or more clear spelling or grammar errors (not names, tools, or US/UK variants) in the headline, About and Experience? (yes = fail)

rules.statement: No placeholder or broken text: no 'Lorem', '[Company]', 'TBD', duplicated paragraphs, or text pasted with broken bullets or encoding.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: placeholder regex, duplicate-paragraph detection, mojibake check.

rules.statement: Advisory (weight 0): a recent photo of the student alone is on the profile. Placed never assesses the photo's appearance, dress, background or 'professionalism' and never runs face analysis. The only checks are the user's own answers ('Is it a recent photo of you?').
rules.tip: Use a recent photo of just you. Placed never looks at or judges your photo.
rules.evidenceNote: Careers-service consensus to have a photo: B; 'must be your likeness' is LinkedIn policy: A. Photo effects on raters are evidence of bias, not validity (Baert; Roulin & Levashina).
rules.notes: 01, 06, 08 and 09 wanted photo scored (major) and in places vision-judged for dress. Overruled on fairness grounds (see playbook §8). Marketing's custom-banner bonus becomes a tip.

rules.statement: Advisory (weight 0): when actively applying, Open to Work is set to 'Recruiters only' with target job titles (sector titles from the keyword bank), UK locations and start dates. The public #OpenToWork frame is the student's choice and is never scored.
rules.tip: When you're applying, turn on Open to Work for recruiters only, with your target roles, UK locations and start date. The public green frame is up to you.
rules.evidenceNote: Mechanism: A (LinkedIn Help). Effect: B (LinkedIn's own 37% InMail-response figure, global, response not hiring).
rules.notes: Warn if the public frame is on while the user lists a current internship (LinkedIn 'can't guarantee complete privacy').

rules.statement: Advisory (weight 0): at least one recommendation from a manager, supervisor, lecturer, society lead or client that names specific work.
rules.tip: A recommendation from a manager, lecturer, society lead or client that names specific work you did carries weight.
rules.notes: Research and marketing researchers wanted it major for final/masters; kept advisory because the count depends on network (fairness) and the PDF may not carry recommendations.

rules.statement: Advisory risk check (weight 0): recent public posts, comments or photos contain nothing the student would be uncomfortable with an interviewer reading (abuse, discriminatory content, explicit images, confidential employer information). Political or religious views alone are not a fail. Posting nothing passes.
rules.tip: Before applying, skim your recent posts, comments and photos: anything you wouldn't want an interviewer to read? Posting nothing is fine.
rules.evidenceNote: 02: B for 'check your footprint' advice; C for magnitude (US/old vendor surveys).
rules.llmGuidance: Would a reasonable UK graduate recruiter find anything in these posts unprofessional (abuse, discriminatory content, explicit or drunken images, confidential employer info)? Political or religious views alone are not a fail.
rules.passExample: Reshares of society events; a thank-you post after an insight day.
rules.failExample: A post mocking a named recruiter; an office photo with a client document visible.
rules.notes: Shown more prominently for final/masters. The 'activity in last 90 days' check from LI-GEN-18 is dropped: no evidence posting helps students.

rules.statement: Advisory (weight 0): a deliberate network of relevant connections (course mates, colleagues, society members, alumni at target employers; at least ~50, 20 for 1st years) and follows target firms. Coaching only; never ranked against peers.
rules.tip: Connect with course mates, colleagues, society members and alumni at firms you're targeting (around 50 is a good start; 20 in first year), and follow those firms.
rules.evidenceNote: Networking value: A (careers-service consensus); thresholds: C/D. Network size tracks income, race and gender (LinkedIn Economic Graph), so weight 0.
rules.notes: Consulting penultimate: nudge outreach to alumni before the Nov-Jan application windows; finance: ask the user to name 3 professionals contacted this term (coaching).

rules.statement: Advisory (weight 0): a verification badge (identity via Persona passport, or education/workplace where offered).
rules.tip: If LinkedIn offers it, verify your identity, school or workplace to get the verification badge.
rules.evidenceNote: Mechanism A; LinkedIn's '60% more profile views' is its own claim with no method (B).

rules.statement: GitHub or portfolio link visible in Contact info (websites), About or Featured.
rules.llmGuidance: Regex github.com/<user>, gitlab.com/, devpost.com/, *.vercel.app or a personal domain in the export's Contact block or Summary. If absent from the PDF, ask whether it is in Featured (paste the URL).

rules.statement: Headline = degree/year/university + specialism or stack + target: at least one tech term from the keyword bank and a target (role type and/or season); not just 'Student at X'.
rules.llmGuidance: Code checks a tech term and a target pattern (intern|internship|placement|graduate|SWE|software engineer|20\d\d) and rejects ^student at. Then: does the headline tell a recruiter what this student builds and what role they want?
rules.passExample: '2nd-year CS @ UCL | Go, Python, PostgreSQL | Seeking 2027 SWE internships'
rules.failExample: 'Student at UCL'

rules.statement: No self-awarded professional titles in the headline or project labels: 'Software Engineer', 'Full-Stack Developer', 'AI/ML Engineer', 'CTO' or 'Founder' only when backed by a real role (employer, dates, description). Personal projects are labelled as projects.
rules.llmGuidance: Is every professional job title used in the headline or project labels backed by a real role (employer, dates, description), rather than a personal or course project?
rules.passExample: 'Software Engineering Intern · Monzo · Jun-Sep 2026'
rules.failExample: Headline 'Full-Stack Developer | AI/ML Engineer | Cloud Architect' with only a to-do-app project.
rules.notes: Experience-entry mislabelling is LI-GEN-02 (critical); this rule covers self-descriptive labels.

rules.statement: At least 2 technical projects visible (Projects section, Experience entries or Featured), each with stack, own role, one outcome and a link.
rules.evidenceNote: 03: B; researcher set critical when there is no tech experience and no projects. Editor kept major (critical reserved for integrity); the dimension weight (proof 35) already makes it decisive.
rules.llmGuidance: Count project entries. For each: does this project say what was built, with what stack, by whom (solo or team of N), and with what result? Masters: a dissertation or MSc group project counts.
rules.passExample: 'Built a Flask + PostgreSQL ticketing app for CompSoc; 1,200 users, 4,000 tickets sold; solo; repo link'
rules.failExample: 'Website project using HTML'
rules.notes: The Projects section is probably not in the PDF: tell students to mirror 2 lines per project into About/Experience.

rules.statement: Featured holds at least one technical artefact (repo, live demo, Devpost, technical write-up), not only certificates or announcement posts.
rules.evidenceNote: 03: B/D. Lower used.
rules.llmGuidance: Does Featured contain at least one item that shows code or a working product? Not applicable without a screenshot or pasted link.
rules.passExample: Pinned GitHub repo with README + live demo link.
rules.failExample: Only a LinkedIn Learning certificate image.

rules.statement: The top skills the export shows (the ~3 LinkedIn lists first) are technical and relevant (languages, frameworks, CS fundamentals), not office tools or generic soft skills.
rules.evidenceNote: 03: B/D. Lower used. Audit 2026-10-18 (docs/research/audit-2026-10-18/08-linkedin.md): minor/D until real exports confirm what the PDF Top Skills sidebar reflects; LinkedIn Help describes reordering and About 'Top skills', not pinning.
rules.llmGuidance: Top Skills from the export vs keyword bank; fail if any of the 3 is in the noise list (Microsoft Office, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Communication, Teamwork, Leadership, Social Media). Excel allowed for fintech data roles only.

rules.statement: Listed languages and frameworks are evidenced: each technical skill in Top Skills (and any the user pastes) appears in at least one Experience, Project or Education description.
rules.llmGuidance: Is each listed language or framework shown in use in Experience, Projects, Education or About (synonyms count)? More than half unevidenced = fail; a quarter to a half = partial.

rules.statement: Tech Experience entries use X-Y-Z content: action, stack and a measurable or concrete result, with the student's own contribution clear. Not blank, not a duty list.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: description present + at least one number or result word + at least one tech term. Then: does this entry say what the student personally built or changed, with what tools, and what happened as a result?
rules.passExample: 'Cut API p95 latency from 800ms to 220ms by adding Redis caching (Python, FastAPI)'
rules.failExample: 'Worked on the backend team. Attended stand-ups.'

rules.statement: Non-tech roles are kept but short: 1-2 lines with one transferable outcome; not deleted, not padded to tech length.
rules.llmGuidance: Code flags non-tech roles over ~600 chars. LLM: does this non-tech entry give one transferable outcome in 1-2 lines?
rules.passExample: 'Handled 100+ customers per shift on weekends; trained 3 new starters on the till system.'
rules.failExample: A 7-line duty list for a retail job.

rules.statement: About is specific: names what the student builds, at least one project or role with a number, a target role and timeframe, and links. ~600-1,200 characters.
rules.evidenceNote: 03: C/D. Lower used.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: length band, a number, a link. Then: could this About only describe this student (specific projects, stack, target), rather than any CS student?
rules.passExample: 'I build backend services... my CompSoc ticketing app served 1,200 students... looking for 2027 SWE internships in London.'
rules.failExample: 'Passionate, driven CS student eager to leverage cutting-edge technologies.'

rules.statement: Education carries SWE signal: expected graduation date, 3-6 relevant modules and/or the group or final-year project with stack, and the grade or a year average if 2:1 or above (optional below that; a missing grade is never a fail).
rules.llmGuidance: Code: grade regex (First|2:1|2\.1|\d{2}%); module keywords (Algorithms, Operating Systems, Databases, Distributed, Compilers, Machine Learning, Software Engineering). 1st year: grade optional. Masters: dissertation title expected.

rules.statement: Tech activities are named with role or result: hackathons, tech societies, competitive programming, open source, TA/tutoring.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: keywords (hackathon, Devpost, ICPC, UKIEPC, Advent of Code, open source, pull request, CompSoc, TA) in Experience/Summary/Honors. LLM: is a role or result stated ('organiser', '3rd of 60', 'merged PR'), not just 'member'?
rules.passExample: 'Hackathon 2nd of 38 teams (Mar 2026); built the Python data pipeline.'
rules.failExample: 'Member, Computing Society.'
rules.notes: Researcher: major for 1st year and penultimate without an internship; minor otherwise.

rules.statement: Certifications are signal, not noise: cloud vendor exams are a small plus; more than 3 short completion certificates with fewer than 2 described projects is flagged.
rules.llmGuidance: Classify the export's Certifications list (vendor exam vs completion certificate); flag if completion certs > 3 and projects < 2.

rules.statement: Competitive programming / LeetCode is stated as a verifiable result (contest rank, rating, ICPC regional placing), not as a problem count in the headline.
rules.llmGuidance: If the profile mentions competitive programming or LeetCode, is it stated as a verifiable result (contest rank, rating, ICPC placing) rather than a problem count? Not applicable when it isn't mentioned.
rules.passExample: 'UKIEPC 2025: 14th of 90 teams'
rules.failExample: Headline 'Solved 600+ LeetCode problems'

rules.statement: Advisory risk check (weight 0): activity is neutral-to-technical. No posting is fine; technical write-ups are good; engagement-bait or unprofessional posts are flagged.
rules.tip: You don't need to post. Technical write-ups help; engagement-bait doesn't.
rules.evidenceNote: 03: C/D. Lower used.
rules.llmGuidance: Do the visible posts show the student's own technical work or learning, rather than engagement-bait or hype? Never fail a profile for having no posts.
rules.passExample: 'What I learned scaling RoomFinder to 900 users' with a repo link.
rules.failExample: 'I'm thrilled to announce I solved my 500th LeetCode problem 🚀 Agree?'

rules.statement: Headline names a data target role or function (data analyst/scientist, BI, analytics, insight, data engineering) or a quantitative degree, and at least 2 concrete tools (SQL, Python, R, Excel, Power BI, Tableau...).
rules.evidenceNote: 04: B/D. Lower used. 1st year: one tool is enough.
rules.llmGuidance: Regex role lexicon + tool lexicon. If ambiguous: does the headline state a data-related target role/degree AND at least two named tools?
rules.passExample: 'Stats @ UCL | Aspiring Data Analyst | SQL · Python · Power BI'
rules.failExample: 'Student at UCL | Hardworking and passionate'

rules.statement: Headline does not present the student as holding a data job title they have not held ('Data Scientist', 'ML Engineer' with no data role). 'Aspiring', 'Student' or a real 'Incoming X Intern at Y' are fine.
rules.evidenceNote: 04: C/D. Lower used.
rules.llmGuidance: Extract titles from the headline and compare with Experience titles. Does the headline present the person as holding a data job title not supported by their Experience section? (yes = fail)
rules.passExample: 'Incoming Data Analyst Intern @ Sky (Summer 2027)' with a matching offer.
rules.failExample: 'Data Scientist | ML Engineer' when Experience shows only a retail job.

rules.statement: SQL is listed as a skill and, for DA/BI targets, shows among the top skills LinkedIn lists first.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: 'SQL' or a dialect (PostgreSQL, MySQL, T-SQL, BigQuery) in Top Skills / Skills / About.
rules.evidenceNote: Audit 2026-10-18 (docs/research/audit-2026-10-18/08-linkedin.md): minor/D until real exports confirm what the PDF Top Skills sidebar reflects.

rules.statement: At least one of Python or R is listed, and at least one visualisation/BI tool (Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Excel charts).
rules.llmGuidance: Code: lexicon match across Skills/About/Experience.

rules.statement: Top skills are evidenced: each of the top 5 skills appears in at least one Experience, Project or About sentence that shows it in use.
rules.evidenceNote: 04: B/C. Lower used.
rules.llmGuidance: For each of the top 5 skills, is there a sentence showing the user applied it to a task (not a bare mention)?
rules.passExample: Skill 'SQL' + project bullet 'Wrote SQL joins across 3 ONS tables...'
rules.failExample: Skills 'TensorFlow, Spark, Hadoop' with no description mentioning any of them.

rules.statement: Skills list is focused: 8-30 skills, and fewer than about a third are generic non-data traits ('Teamwork', 'Microsoft Word').
rules.evidenceNote: 04: C/D. Lower used.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: count + generic-skill blacklist. Not applicable with PDF only (the export shows ~3 Top Skills).

rules.statement: Portfolio link present: at least one link to GitHub, Tableau Public, Kaggle, Power BI web, Observable/Streamlit or a personal site, in Contact websites, About, Projects or Featured.
rules.evidenceNote: 04: A ('standard practice in the sector'). Researcher set critical for penultimate/final/masters; editor kept major (critical reserved for integrity). Proof weight 33 keeps it decisive.
rules.llmGuidance: Code: a URL on a known portfolio host or a personal site in the Contact websites or About. Presence only: Placed does not check the link is reachable.

rules.statement: At least one project follows question -> data -> method -> result, with a number or decision in the result.
rules.llmGuidance: Is there a project description that states the question asked, the data used, the method applied and a concrete result?
rules.passExample: 'Asked whether A&E waits rose after 2022; merged NHS England monthly data (3.2m rows) in SQL; regression; waits rose 14% in winter months; dashboard on Tableau Public.'
rules.failExample: 'Data analysis project using Python and pandas.'

rules.statement: Portfolio is not only tutorial datasets (Titanic, Iris, MNIST, Boston housing) with no original question.
rules.evidenceNote: 04: C, practitioner consensus (bootcamp/blog sources, not cited individually).
rules.llmGuidance: Lexicon of tutorial datasets; then: are all listed projects based on standard tutorial datasets with no original question? (yes = fail)
rules.passExample: A project on TfL bike-hire data asking about weather effects.
rules.failExample: Only 'Titanic survival prediction' and 'Iris classification'.

rules.statement: Communication evidence exists: at least one item shows presenting or explaining findings to non-technical people.
rules.llmGuidance: Does the profile show the user communicating data findings to a non-technical audience?
rules.passExample: 'Presented churn findings to 4 store managers; recommendation adopted.'
rules.failExample: Only technical tool lists.

rules.statement: Education lists quantitative modules and/or a data-heavy dissertation; a grade or average is a plus if 2:1 or above (optional: a missing grade is never a fail).
rules.llmGuidance: Does the Education entry list quantitative modules (statistics, econometrics, machine learning, databases, probability, operational research) or a data-heavy dissertation? A quantitative degree title with no modules is partial. A missing grade is never a fail; judge non-UK grading systems on their own terms.

rules.statement: Certifications are signal, not noise: at most ~6 listed; if more than 3, at least one is a proctored/vendor cert (PL-300, Tableau, AWS/Azure/GCP) or tied to a project; none expired.
rules.llmGuidance: Count + recognised-cert lexicon + expiry date parse. Masters: Google Data Analytics alone does not count as a differentiator (looks junior).

rules.statement: Non-data jobs show a data or quant angle where truthful: for retail/hospitality/tutoring roles, at least one bullet mentions a number, a tool or a process improvement.
rules.evidenceNote: 04: B/D. Lower used. Final/masters: skip when relevant data experience exists (checker condition).
rules.llmGuidance: For non-data roles, does at least one bullet show numeracy, a tool or a measurable improvement? Never reward invented analysis.
rules.passExample: 'Tracked weekly waste in Excel; cut over-ordering 10%.'
rules.failExample: 'Served customers and handled the till.'

rules.statement: About is specific: names a target role, 2+ tools in context and at least one result; at most 2 clichés ('passionate about data', 'data-driven', 'turning data into insights', 'lifelong learner').
rules.llmGuidance: Cliché regex + LLM: does the About section give a target role, tools used in context and at least one concrete result?
rules.passExample: 'Second-year Economics student... I use SQL and Python (pandas)... rail punctuality vs weather: each 10mm of rain cut on-time arrivals by ~2.3 points...'
rules.failExample: 'Passionate, data-driven student eager to turn data into actionable insights.'

rules.statement: Advisory risk check (weight 0): posting is optional; if posts exist they share real work and contain no AI-generic 'tips' content or employer data.
rules.tip: Posting is optional. If you post, share real work, not generic AI-written tips, and never employer data.
rules.llmGuidance: Are recent posts about the user's own projects/learning rather than generic tips or engagement bait? Never penalise zero posts.
rules.passExample: 'I mapped London bike-hire demand vs rainfall; 3 takeaways + link.'
rules.failExample: '🚀 10 Python tricks every data analyst MUST know 👇'

rules.statement: At least one data/measurement skill is evidenced (GA4, Excel analysis, A/B test, survey analysis, SQL, Looker Studio) in an experience or project, not only listed.
rules.llmGuidance: Does the profile show the student measuring a marketing result with data, not just creating content? Researcher: major for growth/performance targets (needs the sub-area question).
rules.passExample: 'Set up GA4 events for the society site; found 70% mobile drop-off at checkout and fixed the form, lifting ticket conversion from 2.3% to 3.9%'
rules.failExample: Skills list says 'Google Analytics' with no use anywhere.

rules.statement: Certifications are relevant and proportionate: from the worth-listing set (Google Digital Marketing, GA4, Google Ads, HubSpot, Meta Blueprint, CIM) or clearly relevant; certs at most 2x the number of marketing-relevant entries and at most ~8 in total.
rules.llmGuidance: Parse Certifications, whitelist match, ratio. 1st year: skip the ratio check.

rules.statement: No AI-generic or cliché-saturated copy across headline, About and experience: most sentences carry specific details (names, numbers, platforms, outcomes).
rules.llmGuidance: Cliché-list density (passionate, driven, dynamic, leverage, synergy, storyteller, results-driven, innovative, 🚀) over threshold; LLM: does the profile contain specific details in most sentences rather than generic buzzwords?
rules.passExample: Sentences anchored in named campaigns and numbers.
rules.failExample: 'Leveraging innovative strategies to drive impactful results in a dynamic landscape.'

rules.statement: Recent posts, when present, are substantive portfolio pieces: campaign breakdowns, project results with what was learned, event write-ups with an insight. Zero posts = not applicable, never a fail. Engagement-bait fails.
rules.evidenceNote: 09: B. Marketing is the only archetype where posts count as proof (portfolio), not just risk.
rules.llmGuidance: Do the student's recent posts show marketing thinking (an insight, result or analysis) rather than generic announcements or bait?
rules.passExample: 'Why Surreal's billboard campaign works: 3 things I'd steal for our society freshers push...'
rules.failExample: 'Agree? 👇 Comment YES if you believe in hustle!'

rules.statement: Evidence of sector interest beyond coursework: competitions (e.g. L'Oréal Brandstorm), virtual experiences, sector events, following/engaging with brands or agencies.
rules.llmGuidance: Keyword bank (competition, Brandstorm, Forage, virtual experience, Advertising Unlocked, society) + LLM: does the profile show at least one marketing activity the student chose to do outside their degree?
rules.passExample: 'Finalist, L'Oréal Brandstorm UK 2026' / 'Unilever marketing virtual experience: built a launch plan for a Dove line extension'
rules.failExample: No marketing activity outside required modules.

rules.statement: Headline names a research area and at least one method or tool, not only 'Student at X'.
rules.llmGuidance: Regex for a degree/institution-only headline; LLM: does the headline name a specific research area/question AND at least one method, tool or technique?
rules.passExample: 'MSc Statistics, UCL | Causal inference for health data | R, Stan'
rules.failExample: 'Student at University of Manchester'

rules.statement: No over-claiming self-labels: 'Researcher', 'Scientist', 'Research Scientist', 'Published Author' in the headline or titles are backed by a matching role or output.
rules.evidenceNote: 10: D, critical. Editor set major for self-labels (consistent with SWE/data/product); Experience mislabelling is LI-GEN-02 (critical) and fabricated outputs surface through LI-GEN-01 and LI-RESEARCH-06.
rules.llmGuidance: Is every research-type title backed by a listed role or output that justifies it?
rules.passExample: 'Summer Research Intern, Dept of Physics, Durham (8 wks)'
rules.failExample: Headline 'AI Researcher' with no research role or output anywhere.

rules.statement: About states a research interest as a question or problem, plus evidence, plus direction (100-250 words).
rules.llmGuidance: Does the About contain (a) a specific research interest, (b) at least one concrete piece of evidence (project/method/output), and (c) a stated direction (e.g. PhD in X / RA roles)? 1st year: (c) optional.
rules.passExample: 'I'm interested in why wage growth stalled after 2008... In my dissertation I used Labour Force Survey microdata in Stata to... I'm applying for economics PhDs and policy research roles.'
rules.failExample: 'Passionate, curious student who loves learning and research.'

rules.statement: Research Experience entries describe question -> method -> finding/output.
rules.llmGuidance: For each research-type entry, are the method used and the output/finding both stated? Not applicable when there are no research entries.
rules.passExample: 'Built a Python pipeline to clean 40k survey responses; ran fixed-effects regressions; findings presented in lab meeting.'
rules.failExample: 'Assisted with research in the lab.'

rules.statement: Individual contribution is explicit on any co-authored or team research.
rules.llmGuidance: Does each co-authored output or team project state what the student personally did?
rules.passExample: 'Co-author (3rd of 5): built the simulation and wrote the methods section.'
rules.failExample: 'Co-authored a paper on protein folding.'

rules.statement: Publications section is honest and well-formed: each item has a venue/type, date, status (published / preprint / submitted / in prep) and a link or DOI where one exists; coursework is not listed as a publication.
rules.evidenceNote: 10: B; researcher: critical if fabricated or mislabelled. Placed cannot verify fabrication; a CV contradiction escalates via LI-GEN-01.
rules.llmGuidance: Is every Publications item a genuine research output with venue/type, date and status, and none of them coursework? Not applicable when the section is empty.
rules.passExample: 'Poster: "X", UCL Undergraduate Research Conference, Jun 2026'
rules.failExample: 'Essay on Keynesian economics, 2025'

rules.statement: At least one research-evidence item (dissertation, UROP or placement, independent project with method, poster, preprint, competition write-up) appears in Experience, Projects, Publications or Featured.
Scholarly identity is linked when the student has any output or code: ORCID iD and/or Google Scholar / GitHub / personal site in Contact info or About.
rules.llmGuidance: Regex orcid.org/\d{4}-, scholar.google, github.com. Researcher: major if the student has outputs but no link. Never require Google Scholar from undergraduates.

rules.statement: Education includes research-relevant detail: dissertation title and supervisor (final/MSc), 3-5 relevant advanced modules, and the grade or average to date if 2:1/First or equivalent (optional below that; a missing grade is never a fail).
rules.llmGuidance: Does the Education entry include research-relevant detail: 3-5 relevant advanced modules and, for final-year and MSc students, a dissertation title? A grade is a plus if 2:1/First or equivalent; a missing grade is never a fail. 1st year: modules only.

rules.statement: Skills include the core analysis tool for the subfield (Python, R or Stata) plus at least one named method, and these also appear in Experience or Projects.
rules.llmGuidance: Is at least one listed core tool/method also evidenced in an Experience or Projects entry?
rules.passExample: Skills 'Stata, Panel data' + experience 'fixed-effects regressions in Stata'.
rules.failExample: Skills 'Python, Machine Learning, Deep Learning', nothing in experience.

rules.statement: Communication evidence: at least one item shows research communicated (poster, talk, blog explainer, policy brief, outreach, teaching or tutoring).
rules.llmGuidance: Is there at least one item showing research communicated to others? Researcher: major for think-tank targets.
rules.passExample: 'Presented results at the department's undergraduate research seminar (30 attendees).'
rules.failExample: No talk, poster, write-up or teaching anywhere.

rules.statement: Tone is academic-accessible, not hype: no 'revolutionary/groundbreaking/thought leader', no overstated findings.
rules.llmGuidance: Is the About/Experience free of hype language and overstated claims about results?
rules.passExample: 'Found a modest association (r=0.3) between...'
rules.failExample: 'Discovered a groundbreaking link that changes how we think about...'

rules.statement: Featured holds a research artefact (poster PDF, dissertation abstract, repo, explainer) rather than generic certificates or reposts.
rules.llmGuidance: Does Featured contain at least one research artefact made by the student? Not applicable without a screenshot or pasted link.
rules.passExample: Seminar slides PDF + GitHub repo with README.
rules.failExample: Only certificate images.

rules.statement: Advisory risk check (weight 0; prominent for ONS/Civil Service targets): no unpublished or confidential lab data and no partisan content in visible posts.
rules.tip: Keep unpublished or confidential lab data and partisan content out of your posts, especially if you're targeting the ONS or Civil Service.
rules.evidenceNote: 10: A for Civil Service impartiality (applies once employed); D for the data-confidentiality norm. Lower used.
rules.llmGuidance: Do the pasted posts share unpublished data or confidential lab material, or partisan political content (relevant for impartial-sector targets)?
rules.passExample: 'Presented my summer project poster; here's the public preprint.'
rules.failExample: A screenshot of unpublished lab results; a partisan campaign post from someone targeting ONS.

rules.statement: Direction signal: the headline or About says what the student is seeking (PhD area / RA / policy research), not only the Open to Work frame.
rules.llmGuidance: Does the headline or About state what the student is seeking (e.g. 'Applying for PhDs in X, 2027')?
rules.passExample: '...I'm applying for summer research placements in labour economics, then a master's and PhD.'
rules.failExample: No direction stated anywhere.
